one_liner: Zendesk has a broad REST API with self-serve OAuth 2.0 (auth code + PKCE); a free 14-day trial gives working credentials, global OAuth for multi-tenant apps may need Zendesk setup; only community MCP servers found.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code (with PKCE) is the recommended method. API tokens (basic auth email/token:api_token) are being removed: unused tokens deactivate from July 28, 2026 and all stop by April 30, 2027. Multi-customer distribution requires global OAuth clients, which must be requested from Zendesk.
access_notes: A free 14-day trial gives a working account and API. No permanent free tier. Sponsored accounts are reserved for Marketplace partners. Individual developers are directed to their own instances or sandboxes.
blocker_notes: Only a 14-day trial is available without partnership. Multi-tenant distribution needs a global OAuth client, which must be requested from Zendesk. Per-instance OAuth clients are self-serve in Admin Center.

evidence.quote: If you plan on distributing an app, integration, or bot to multiple Zendesk customers, you must use global OAuth tokens to authenticate Zendesk API requests.
The authorization code grant flow is used by developers to get OAuth access tokens to authenticate Zendesk API requests.
Starting July 28, 2026, unused tokens will automatically deactivate. By April 30, 2027, all API tokens will stop working.
You can try out the Zendesk platform with a free, 14-day trial account.
Customer developers or individual private app developers should use their own instances or sandboxes.
Zendesk supports using OAuth access tokens to authenticate API requests.
This server provides a comprehensive integration with Zendesk.
This article covers Zendesk acting as an MCP client.
